topStories.headline: Cole Valley Is Having a Moment — New Shops and Restaurants Are Reshaping the Strip
topStories.dek: An SF Standard feature published September 3 documents the wave of new businesses quietly transforming the neighborhood's compact commercial corridor.
topStories.body:
A deep look at Cole Valley published September 3 by the SF Standard finds the neighborhood's tiny commercial corridor — running about one and a half blocks along Cole Street between Parnassus and Carl — in the middle of a notable revival. The strip already packs nearly a dozen eateries, two coffee shops, a hardware store, an upscale grocer, a gym, and an urgent care center into a remarkably small footprint. What has changed is a rash of new arrivals filling spaces that sat vacant for years.

Pasta Supply Co., the popular pasta counter with outposts in the Richmond and the Mission, is taking over the Cole Street storefront that housed Peet's Coffee for 12 years before its closure in January. Owner Anthony Strong plans to open the third location at 919 Cole St. in October, with fresh pasta made in the window and a few sidewalk tables — the same counter-service format as his other shops. The Infatuation noted this week that Strong crowdfunded the expansion partly by offering donors pasta for life.

Double Black SF, a coffee shop embedded inside outdoor-gear brand Yardsale, opened this spring at 925 Cole St., founded by two former Shark Tank contestants who are themselves Cole Valley residents. Kamekyo, a 28-year-old sushi restaurant, closed earlier this year; the SF Standard reports its former space will be occupied in coming months by a new concept from chef Jiro Lin. Arabic restaurant Beit Rema and the Cole Valley Tavern are also among the recent arrivals drawing foot traffic to the strip.

The Standard quoted a Civic Joy Fund representative saying Cole Valley "might be the most quintessential" of San Francisco's neighborhood villages, and that the small-town feel appears resilient even as new tenants arrive. Residents and longtime merchants told the paper the mood is cautiously optimistic — most of the newcomers are driven by people who already live in the neighborhood.

topStories.headline: 'Forever Grateful, Golden Gate Park' Opens Saturday With the Furthur Bus on Public Display for the First Time
topStories.dek: The Haight Street Art Center's immersive Grateful Dead exhibition opens September 5 at the County Fair Building in Golden Gate Park, anchored by Ken Kesey's legendary bus making its first-ever public appearance.
topStories.body:
One of the most anticipated cultural openings of the fall arrives Saturday, September 5, just down the hill from Haight-Ashbury: the Haight Street Art Center's 'Forever Grateful, Golden Gate Park,' an immersive exhibition running through October 25 at the County Fair Building in Golden Gate Park.

The show is the second and culminating chapter of a two-part tribute to the Grateful Dead. The first exhibition has been running free at the Haight Street Art Center at 215 Haight Street since July 3 and continues through September 20, featuring more than 400 works including posters, handbills, historic instruments, and memorabilia. The Golden Gate Park installment is a different experience — participatory rather than contemplative, according to the organizers.

Its centerpiece is Ken Kesey and the Merry Pranksters' original Furthur bus, on public display for the first time since 1969. The bus traveled to San Francisco from the Kesey family's Oregon farm in mid-August. Jerry Garcia's BMW is also on display. Visitors wind through an environment that includes large-scale projections, puppetry, immersive theater from New York company Third Rail Projects, Lance Gordon of Mad Alchemy's Analog Liquid Light Show, and community storytelling installations. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie announced a free concert tied to the opening.

Kelly Harris, Executive Director of Haight Street Art Center, described the Park site as a homecoming: the exhibition brings visitors "to where so much of the Grateful Dead's history actually happened." Tickets for the Golden Gate Park exhibition are available at haightstreetart.org; the September 5 opening-night fundraiser is separately ticketed.

topStories.headline: Upzoning Is Now Law on Haight and Carl Streets — HANC Turns to a Historic District as a Counterweight
topStories.dek: With the Family Zoning Plan passed in December 2025 allowing buildings up to six stories on Haight and Carl, the Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council is pushing for a broader historic district — and its September meeting will bring a Doolan-Larson House update.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Board of Supervisors passed the Family Zoning Plan 7–4 in December 2025, meeting a state mandate and clearing the way for buildings up to six stories on neighborhood commercial corridors — including Haight Street and Carl Street, which previously maxed out at four stories. The rezoning also allows up to 16 stories on Market Street. Mission Local noted in an August 2026 district election preview that the vote remains a live issue in the upcoming District 8 race, with candidates split on whether the plan does enough to protect renters.

For the Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council, the law's passage has sharpened the urgency of a parallel strategy: creating a formal historic district. The HANC website notes that "our impetus and urgency comes from the recent upzoning — one- and two-story buildings are now targets for demolition," and that landmarks and historic districts can slow demolitions. The city's Planning Department has released survey findings defining a Haight-Ashbury Historic District based on its Counterculture Context Statement, but HANC argues the scope is too narrow — limited to Haight Street and a small section of Stanyan, and only covering the period 1965 to 1975. HANC wants the district to encompass a broader area and longer timeline, pointing to records such as a bread line on Clayton Street from 1906.

The September HANC meeting — details going out in the HANC Voice newsletter, which HANC says will be mailed and emailed around September 4 — is also expected to include a presentation from Ted Lieser of San Francisco Heritage on the Doolan-Larson House, the landmark Colonial Revival building at the northwest corner of Haight and Ashbury. Three development teams submitted final proposals on June 12 to reimagine the property as a public cultural facility; SF Heritage said it intended to select a partner during the summer of 2026. As of this week, no selection had been publicly announced. HANC meets the second Thursday of each month at 7 p.m. at the Park Branch Library, 1833 Page Street.

events.description: The annual Cole Valley street fair, back for its 21st year, brings arts, crafts, food, and community to the neighborhood's main commercial strip. Dogs on leashes welcome; Muni lines 7, 37, 43, 66, and N serve the area.

moreNews.headline: PG&E Outage Darkens Haight-Ashbury and Western Addition in Year's Sixth Major Blackout
moreNews.body: An unplanned PG&E power outage struck Haight-Ashbury, the Western Addition, and surrounding neighborhoods on August 29, 2026 — the sixth significant citywide outage of the year, according to Hoodline. The blackout came just days after a separate August 13 outage had hit the Outer Sunset and Lakeshore, and two weeks after a fifth outage darkened Russian Hill, North Beach, and Chinatown on August 10. Residents can check PG&E's Outage Center online or call 1-800-743-5002 for real-time updates; the city's AlertSF text notification system also covers outage alerts.

moreNews.headline: Doolan-Larson House Partner Selection Still Pending After June Proposal Deadline
moreNews.body: San Francisco Heritage received final proposals from three development teams on June 12, 2026 for the future of the landmark Doolan-Larson House and Storefronts at the corner of Haight and Ashbury streets. The nonprofit, which inherited the 1903 Colonial Revival building from Norm Larson upon his death in 2018, has been seeking a partner to transform the 7,500-square-foot property into a public-serving cultural facility honoring the neighborhood's counterculture history. Heritage said in June it intended to select a partner during the summer of 2026; as of this week that announcement had not been made. HANC's September meeting is expected to include an update on the process from Ted Lieser of SF Heritage.

restaurants.name: Cha Cha Cha
restaurants.description: A Haight Street institution since 1984 serving bold Caribbean-Latin tapas — jerk chicken, ropa vieja, Cajun shrimp, paella — alongside legendary sangria in a lively, colorful dining room.

restaurants.name: Zazie
restaurants.description: A beloved Cole Valley neighborhood bistro specializing in Southern French country cooking, known for all-day brunch, a seasonal dinner menu, and a heated garden patio; proudly tip-free with living wages for all staff.

restaurants.name: Magnolia Brewing
restaurants.description: A revived Haight Street craft brewery and pub — founded in 1997 and reopened under new local ownership in December 2024 — serving house-brewed beers, a full cocktail bar, and pub fare in a wide-windowed corner taproom at Haight and Masonic.

restaurants.name: Toronado
restaurants.description: A legendary Lower Haight craft beer mecca open since 1987, now under new local ownership, pouring roughly 50 rotating taps in a cash-only, no-frills setting beloved by serious beer drinkers worldwide.

restaurants.name: The Alembic
restaurants.description: A cozy Upper Haight institution known for meticulously crafted cocktails, an extensive American whiskey selection, and a creative small-plates menu ideal for date nights.

restaurants.name: Mad Dog in the Fog
restaurants.description: A beloved San Francisco British pub — relocated from the Lower Haight to the Upper Haight in 2022 and the namesake of Train's new album — offering imported beers, pub grub, and multiple TVs for sports at Haight and Clayton.

restaurants.name: O'Reilly's of Haight Street
restaurants.type: Irish pub and live music venue
restaurants.description: A lively Irish pub at the western end of Haight-Ashbury offering nightly live music, big-screen sports, Guinness on tap, and a warm neighborhood vibe with a traditional fireplace.

restaurants.name: Stoa Bar
restaurants.description: A relaxed Lower Haight neighborhood bar open Monday through Saturday from 4 p.m., serving food alongside craft drinks in a convivial setting at the corner of Haight and Pierce.

restaurants.name: Parada 22
restaurants.description: A veteran-owned Haight Street gem serving authentic Puerto Rican cuisine — mofongo, pernil, tostones — in a colorful dining room with Caribbean cocktails.

restaurants.name: Sandy's
restaurants.description: A popular Upper Haight sandwich counter known for its acclaimed New Orleans-style muffulettas and other hearty sandwiches, drawing loyal lunch crowds of neighborhood regulars.

restaurants.name: Dumpling Union
restaurants.description: The Lower Haight outpost of this popular dim sum spot at Haight and Steiner, serving pillowy bao, expertly crafted xiao long bao, siu mai, and beef chow mein in a casual, walk-in-friendly setting.

restaurants.name: Noc Noc
restaurants.description: A funky, cave-like Lower Haight bar with a grotto-style interior, strong craft cocktails, local beer on tap, and an enduring following for its creative, irreverent atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Zam Zam
restaurants.description: One of San Francisco's most storied dive bars — a Haight Street legacy business open since 1941 — serving no-nonsense martinis and classic cocktails in a Moorish-themed room with an old-school ethos.

restaurants.name: Cole Valley Tavern
restaurants.description: A reliable Cole Valley corner bar and restaurant at Cole and Carl serving inventive cocktails and West Coast comfort food, a neighborhood go-to for locals and N-Judah commuters alike.

restaurants.name: Beit Rima
restaurants.description: The Cole Valley outpost of the acclaimed Lebanese-inspired restaurant, serving outstanding mezze, shawarma, and seasonal Middle Eastern dishes in a calm, intimate setting.

restaurants.name: Finnegans Wake
restaurants.description: A laid-back Cole Valley Irish bar with a spacious, popular patio ideal for groups, offering draft beers and a warm neighborhood atmosphere on Cole Street.

restaurants.name: Bambino's Ristorante
restaurants.description: A charming old-school Italian trattoria in Cole Valley serving hearty pastas, risotto, and classic mains in a cozy, family-friendly dining room.

restaurants.name: Kezar Pub
restaurants.description: A lively Cole Valley sports bar with celebrated chicken wings, plentiful seating, and a wall of big-screen TVs, beloved by locals for game nights and casual dining.

restaurants.name: Crepes on Cole
restaurants.description: A beloved Cole Valley crêperie serving sweet and savory crêpes for breakfast and lunch, with sidewalk seating and a warm neighborhood feel that has made it a local staple for decades.

restaurants.name: Ritual Coffee Roasters
restaurants.description: One of San Francisco's premier specialty coffee roasters, with a Haight Street café serving single-origin pour-overs, espresso drinks, and pastries in a sleek, light-filled space.

hotels.name: Metro Hotel
hotels.description: A comfortable, well-priced boutique hotel in the Lower Haight with a charming garden courtyard, individually decorated rooms, and easy walkability to Haight Street dining and Divisadero transit.

hotels.name: Stanyan Park Hotel
hotels.description: A registered San Francisco historic landmark built in 1905, sitting directly across from Golden Gate Park, offering gracious Victorian-era rooms and suites within easy reach of Haight Street and Cole Valley.

hotels.name: Red Victorian
hotels.description: A revived Haight Street landmark with boutique hotel rooms, a ground-floor café, and a community gathering space honoring the neighborhood's countercultural spirit and history.

hotels.name: The Haight Ashbury Inn
hotels.description: A charming Victorian bed and breakfast steps from the iconic Haight-Ashbury intersection, offering cozy rooms in a historic building with a quintessential neighborhood setting.

shops.name: Booksmith
shops.description: A beloved Haight Street independent bookstore since 1976, now at 1727 Haight, offering a well-curated selection of new books and hosting regular author events that anchor the neighborhood's literary life.

shops.name: Amoeba Music
shops.description: One of the world's great independent music stores — occupying a former bowling alley on Haight Street — stocking a vast selection of new and used vinyl, CDs, DVDs, and music memorabilia across every genre.

shops.name: Piedmont Boutique
shops.description: A Haight Street landmark since 1972, famous for theatrical costumes, festival wear, and an outrageous window display of giant fishnet-clad legs that has become an unofficial neighborhood icon.

shops.name: Love on Haight
shops.description: A Haight Street institution offering hand-dyed and colorful clothing, accessories, and locally designed apparel that keeps the neighborhood's countercultural fashion spirit alive.

shops.name: FTC Skateboarding
shops.description: San Francisco's most iconic skate shop, a Haight Street institution since 1986 that stocks boards, shoes, and apparel while remaining a cornerstone of the city's skateboarding culture.

shops.name: San Franpsycho
shops.description: A homegrown Haight Street clothing brand and boutique celebrating San Francisco's neighborhoods and culture through original graphic tees, hoodies, hats, and accessories.

shops.name: San Francisco Mercantile — Welcome Haight & Ashbury
shops.type: Counterculture gift shop and welcome center
shops.description: A partnership between SF Mercantile and San Francisco Heritage in the historic Doolan-Larson Building at Haight and Ashbury, celebrating neighborhood history with locally made gifts, books, art, and memorabilia.

shops.name: The Love of Ganesha
shops.description: A beloved Haight-Ashbury gift shop stocking incense, crystals, spiritual decor, and an eclectic range of goods reflecting the neighborhood's mystical and countercultural sensibility.

shops.name: Mendels Art and Craft Supplies
shops.description: A Haight Street legacy business offering art supplies, fabrics, and craft materials — a long-time resource for artists, costumers, and makers in the neighborhood.

shops.name: Cole Valley Fair
shops.type: Neighborhood gift and home goods shop
shops.description: A charming Cole Valley gift shop offering a curated selection of home goods, greeting cards, toys, and locally crafted gifts that has served the neighborhood for many years.

shops.name: Cole Valley Pets
shops.description: A neighborhood staple in Cole Valley stocking premium pet food, supplies, and accessories for dogs and cats, with knowledgeable staff and a loyal local following.

artEntertainment.name: Haight Street Art Center
artEntertainment.description: A vibrant Lower Haight gallery and printmaking studio celebrating poster art, counterculture history, and community creativity — currently hosting the landmark free 'Forever Grateful' Grateful Dead exhibition through September 20.

artEntertainment.name: The DeLuxe
artEntertainment.description: Haight Street's storied jazz room, reopened in June 2026 after a three-year closure, offering nightly live music — jazz, blues, roots, and more — in a refurbished Art Deco interior at Haight and Clayton.

artEntertainment.name: O'Reilly's of Haight Street
artEntertainment.description: A dedicated live music venue inside an Irish pub, with nightly performances ranging from folk and rock to singer-songwriters at the western end of Haight-Ashbury.

artEntertainment.name: Amoeba Music
artEntertainment.type: Music store and in-store performance venue
artEntertainment.description: Beyond its role as a legendary record store, Amoeba regularly hosts free in-store performances, listening parties, and special events in its enormous Haight Street space.

artEntertainment.name: Madrone Art Bar
artEntertainment.description: A Lower Haight bar that doubles as a rotating gallery space and live music room, known for eclectic themed nights, local DJs, and a colorful, art-covered interior.

artEntertainment.name: Kezar Stadium
artEntertainment.description: A historic 10,000-seat open-air stadium at the southeastern corner of Golden Gate Park, home to San Francisco City FC soccer and a wide range of community sports, track, and cultural events.

artEntertainment.name: Kezar Pavilion
artEntertainment.description: A 4,000-seat indoor arena adjacent to Kezar Stadium in Golden Gate Park, hosting basketball, volleyball, boxing, roller derby, concerts, and community events year-round.

artEntertainment.name: Park Branch Library
artEntertainment.type: Public library and community gathering space
artEntertainment.description: The Haight-Ashbury branch of the San Francisco Public Library at 1833 Page Street, a community hub for neighborhood meetings, readings, HANC gatherings, and public programs.

gymsRecreation.name: HAUM Studios — Haight-Ashbury
gymsRecreation.description: A serene, community-centered yoga studio at 780 Stanyan Street across from Golden Gate Park, offering Hatha, Vinyasa, Restorative, Yin, and sound bath classes in a space formerly known as Yoga Tree.

gymsRecreation.name: BODYROK Haight
gymsRecreation.description: A Haight-Ashbury studio offering 45-minute pilates-inspired full-body strength training classes on reformer machines, suitable for all fitness levels.

gymsRecreation.name: The Panhandle
gymsRecreation.description: A beloved three-quarter-mile green corridor running from Stanyan to Baker Street along Oak and Fell, offering walking and bike paths, a renovated playground, the Nate Thurmond basketball court, and shaded picnic areas.
gymsRecreation.address: Oak St & Fell St between Stanyan & Baker

gymsRecreation.name: Buena Vista Park
gymsRecreation.type: Hilltop park and dog play area
gymsRecreation.description: San Francisco's oldest park, a wooded hilltop above Haight-Ashbury with panoramic city views, off-leash dog areas, and winding trails through eucalyptus and redwood groves.
gymsRecreation.address: Haight St & Buena Vista Ave W

gymsRecreation.name: Kezar Stadium Track
gymsRecreation.description: The 400-meter all-weather track at Kezar Stadium is open to the public for walking, jogging, and running when not reserved for events, a favorite among neighborhood fitness regulars.

gymsRecreation.name: Panhandle Playground
gymsRecreation.description: A renovated public playground at Oak and Ashbury in the Panhandle, redesigned as part of the city's Let'sPlaySF! initiative with modern play structures and improved amenities for families.

gymsRecreation.name: Nate Thurmond Basketball Court
gymsRecreation.description: A renovated full-court basketball facility in the Panhandle, named in honor of Golden State Warriors legend Nate Thurmond through a partnership with the Warriors Community Foundation and Good Tidings Foundation.

gymsRecreation.name: CorePower Yoga — Haight
gymsRecreation.description: A well-equipped Haight Street yoga studio offering heated classes including Yoga Sculpt, C2, and Hot Power Fusion in a modern setting.

gymsRecreation.name: Golden Gate Park — Haight Entrance
gymsRecreation.description: The eastern entrance to Golden Gate Park at Stanyan Street puts world-class parkland minutes from Haight and Cole Valley, with bike paths, meadows, the Conservatory of Flowers, Hippie Hill, lawn bowling, and disc golf all within easy reach.
